 moved bytes (see internal_transfer_ship).

functions.name: nft_transfer_call

 still can. A hostile receiver (panics, burns gas, returns junk) leaves
 the ship with the receiver, never lost or duplicated.

functions.doc:

 be owned, unlocked, of the run's variant and current-priced), then

functions.name: resupply_repair
functions.doc:
RoguelikeResupply.resupplyRepair: restore listed roster ships to full

functions.name: retreat_run
functions.doc:
RoguelikeMatch.retreatRun: with a game id, concede that game (which
 ends the run); with 0, abandon the run between fights.

functions.name: retry_resolve
functions.doc:
Permissionless recovery if a resolution receipt failed (e.g. ran out of
 gas). Schedules a NEW self-callback, so the seed still comes from a later
 block the caller can't predict. Ids that are unknown, already resolved,
 or requested in this same block are silently dropped (a griefer racing
 this call can't make it revert). Returns how many ids were scheduled.

functions.doc:
SinglePlayerMatch.takeAITurns: permissionless (anyone may advance the
 AI). The AI is deterministic, so a caller can't steer it; storage growth
 is charged to the match's human (their game, their bytes).

functions.name: timeout_joiner
functions.doc:
Lobbies.timeoutJoiner: the creator kicks a joiner who hasn't submitted
 a fleet within one turn time (a kick penalty applies if the creator had
 already committed theirs).

functions.name: turn_in_cores
functions.doc:
DroneStorefront.turnInCores: burn exactly the next tier's DEC cost for
 +1 permanent free ship per claim.

functions.name: upgrade
functions.doc:
Owner-only code upgrade. The new WASM is the raw call input (not
 JSON). After a real deploy the account's full-access keys are deleted,
 so this is the only way to change the code. Deploys, then runs
 `migrate` in the same follow-up receipt; if migrate fails, the deploy
 action fails with it and the old code stays.
